newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Massive clean-up planned for Sydney Harbour.
newsitem.headline: Massive clean-up planned for Sydney Harbour.

text.p: Australia's biggest state annnounced plans on Saturday for a massive clean-up of Sydney Harbour ahead of the 2000 Olympic Games, saying pollution was turning the famous waterway into a health hazard.
The New South Wales state government said overflows of sewage and storm water from the city's century-old drainage system were often hazardous for swimmers and sailors.
The government invited the private sector to come up with ideas to solve the problem and said it hoped to see improved water quality before Sydney hosts the Olympic games in the year 2000.
"Sydney Harbour is for the world a great symbol. It's a sacred site for all Australians," state Premier Bob Carr told a news conference.
"It's the symbol of Australia overseas. It's where the story of modern Australia began and we want to see it's a sparkling jewel, not a degraded asset."

Carr suggested new waste-water treatment plants could be installed at three major overflow points along the harbour's north shore. "Now, if we clean up those alone we will make a huge improvement to water quality," he said.
Earlier on Saturday, The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported that one plan being considered would cost A$400 million (US$316 million) to overhaul Sydney's ageing sewerage system.
